title: The Sword in the Stone
text:
When King Uther Pendragon died, he left no acknowledged heir, and the barons of Britain could not agree who should rule. At Christmas they gathered in the church in the great city to pray for a sign. When they came out after Mass, they found a block of stone with an anvil on it, and a sword stuck through the anvil. Letters on the sword said that whoever pulled it out would be king by God's choice.

The great lords tried one after another, and none could move it. Then young Arthur, whom everyone took to be the son of the knight Sir Ector and the younger brother of Kay, was sent to fetch a sword for Kay. Unable to find one, he pulled the sword from the stone with ease and brought it to his brother.

The barons were outraged that a boy of no known family should be their king. They demanded more time, and the test was repeated at Candlemas, at Easter and at Pentecost. Each time the lords failed and Arthur drew the sword. In the version by Robert de Boron, Arthur agreed patiently to every delay, and when the lords tested him with rich gifts, he gave them away generously and wisely. At last the common people cried out that they would have Arthur and no other, and he was crowned.
lesson: A position given to you is not the same as authority. When people doubt you, patience and visible fairness can earn what the appointment alone cannot.
people: Arthur, Sir Kay, Sir Ector, the barons, Merlin
source: Robert de Boron, Merlin (c. 1200); Thomas Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur, Book I (1485)
caveat: Arthur is a figure of legend, and the sword in the stone appears first in Robert de Boron, not in earlier Welsh or Latin sources.
